first-couple-ocean-steady.label: First-time couple, wants the ocean, sensitive stomach

Cabin 6218 sits right next to your first choice, same midship advantage on deck 6 with a balcony view. The difference is negligible—book this if 6220 isn't available—but it's equally quiet and equally stable for managing queasiness.

couple-ocean-balcony-treat.label: Couple treating themselves to a great balcony

steerClear.reason: Cabin 6150 is a forward balcony on deck 6, which means you're near the bow where motion can be noticeable in any kind of sea. Forward cabins also pick up more anchor noise and early activity from port, which conflicts with the peace and quiet you're prioritizing.

recommendations.reason: Cabin 1820 is the Royal Loft Suite, the absolute pinnacle on Wonder of the Seas. It's forward on Deck 18, so you get the best views of where the ship is going, plus all the suite perks and space money can buy. This is the one to book first for an anniversary without limits.

Cabin 1830 is an Owners Suite on Deck 18, forward starboard, delivering everything a celebration couple wants—real ocean views, abundant space, and the full suite experience. It sits just aft of the Royal Loft, so you still command the bow while keeping a touch more privacy from the ship's busiest deck areas.

Cabin 1832 is another Owners Suite on Deck 18, but on the port side forward. It offers identical perks and space to 1830, so the choice between them really comes down to which side of the ship you prefer for your ocean view and sunrise watching.

Cabin 1850 is the Ultimate Family Suite aft on Deck 18 starboard—a true signature room with exceptional square footage and all suite benefits. The aft placement means slightly less bow motion and a different perspective of the ocean, perfect if you want the prestige without the forward-facing rush.

Cabin 1712 is a Grand Suite midship on Deck 17, offering more space and suite perks than balcony cabins while costing less than the top-tier Lofts. You sacrifice the highest-level extras but keep the elegant proportions and privacy an anniversary pair deserves.

Cabin 1860 is an Owners Suite aft on Deck 18 starboard, matching the prestige and space of the forward suites. The main difference is it's positioned toward the stern, so you're watching the wake rather than the horizon, but the room itself is every bit as luxurious.

steerClear.reason: Cabin 14226 is a Junior Suite amidships on Deck 14—it has a balcony but lacks the true suite perks and commanding space you'd want for a celebration with no budget ceiling.

Cabin 6240 is a Junior Suite midship on Deck 6—while it has a balcony and is technically a suite, it's one of the smallest suite categories and doesn't deliver the prestige or expansive living you're looking for at your price point.

Cabin 10226 is a Junior Suite on Deck 10—a mid-tier room that splits the difference between stateroom and suite but falls short of the exceptional space and amenities you should expect when cost is no object.
